title: Microbial communities in Ceratina calcarata reared on different diets
description: Microbial communities change throughout the course of bee development and may determine survival success of developing larvae. Here, we compare the microbial communities of Ceratina calcarata small carpenter bees reared from eggs across three treatments. Controls used pollen provisions with maternally collected diverse microbiota. Sterile treatments were exposed to alcohol and germicidal UV light. Probiotic treatments used provisions that were sterilized and supplemented with a known bee beneficial symbiont, Apilactobacillus kunkeei. By comparing the bacterial (16S rRNA), fungal (ITS), and plant (rbcL) communities of adults reared across treatments, we characterized distinct microbial communities across each that suggest the microbiome may be continuously in flux depending on factors such as microbial succession and competition.
